findings.title: SSE stream whose drain never starts keeps its close listeners and response unfinished after shutdown (Servlet adapter skip-drain path; SseRegistry.terminate does not finish it)
findings.description: SseRegistry.terminate() only calls endBy("shutdown") and clearQueue() and says 'Listeners stay with the drain or the abort'. That holds for TinyHttpd, where a skipped drain is always preceded by the core's own DefaultResponse.abort (which runs listeners when !drainStarted). It does not hold for the Servlet adapter: ServletExchange.afterHandler (NaruServe-servlet/.../ServletExchange.java:296-330) skips submitting the drain when the exchange is already aborted or when pool.submit throws RejectedExecutionException, and then calls only ServletExchange.abort() (adapter-level, sets a flag and completes the AsyncContext) plus pool.finish(). The core is never told. Trigger: app.shutdown() while an SSE request is still inside its handler at the stop deadline; ServletAdapter.stop() runs p.shutdownNow(), the handler then returns, afterHandler gets RejectedExecutionException. Result: DefaultSseClient.runListeners() never runs (user onClose cleanup such as unsubscribe never fires, contradicting docs/api/sse.md 'app.shutdown() closes open SSE streams and runs onClose'), DefaultResponse stays STREAMING (no onDone, no access-log line), and the client stays in SseRegistry.open until terminate() clears it without running listeners. The same happens if the container's AsyncListener.onError/onTimeout aborts the exchange before the handler returns.
findings.suggested_fix: In SseRegistry.terminate(), for every client left that is !drainStarted(), call c.endBy("shutdown") then c.runListeners() (and have DefaultResponse finish the stream, e.g. res.sseEnded(null)/abort). Additionally make ServletExchange.afterHandler run d.drain(out) inline on the request thread (it fails at once on the aborted stream) instead of silently returning, so the core always finalizes the stream.
